correctness.rationale: The explicit finite-dimensional family satisfies the \(K\)-g-fusion-frame inequalities exactly, and its frame operator sends \(e_1\) outside \(R(K)\), so the disputed inverse has the wrong domain. For the general repair, the Moore--Penrose identity on \(R(K)\) yields a coercive lower bound for the compression; positivity and self-adjointness then give invertibility and the two reconstruction identities.

evidence: The older \(K\)-frame literature supports invertibility of \(S:R(K)\to S(R(K))\); that statement does not imply \(S(R(K))=R(K)\).
The counterexample has \(S(R(K))=\operatorname{span}\{2e_1+e_2\}\), so the range-to-range theorem is true while Huang--Yang formula (2.10) is undefined at \(e_1\).
The compression \(C=P_{R(K)}S|_{R(K)}\) remains coercive by the lower \(K\)-frame inequality and the Moore--Penrose identity on \(R(K)\).

value.rationale: The published reconstruction formula can be undefined under its stated hypotheses, already in dimension three. The correction is constructive and quantitative: it identifies the canonical compressed operator that always works and gives an explicit inverse-norm bound, avoiding the stronger and unnecessary invariance assumption \(S(R(K))=R(K)\).
